We evaluate a range of accelerators spanning high-end edge GPUs (e.g., NVIDIA Jetson Thor), consumer-grade GPUs commonly used in research experiments (e.g., RTX 4090), and high-end datacenter GPUs, including A100, H100, and B100. The GPUs can be mapped to various inference location as shown in Table 2.

This behavior closely mirrors LLM inference, where the prefill phase (prompt processing) is compute-intensive, while the decode phase (token generation) is memory-bound Patel et al. (2024). Jetson Thor, in contrast to the other evaluated GPUs, relies on LPDDR memory, which prioritizes low power consumption for embedded devices but provides substantially lower bandwidth (270 GB/s) than GDDR on RTX 4090 (1 TB/s) and HBM on B100 (8 TB/s).

B100 sustains 11.7 Hz inference with 1K past timesteps, whereas performance drops to 1.2 Hz at 10K steps, which no longer meets real-time requirements. For Jetson Thor and RTX 4090, real-time performance is only achievable when the context length is limited to roughly 100 timesteps (around 8 Hz).

results.description: Deploy NVIDIA Isaac GR00T 1.7 Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor with TensorRT mixed NVFP4 quantization.
snippets: Checkpoint ──► ONNX (per-component) ──► Calibrate (NVFP4/FP8) ──► TensorRT Engines ──► Inference · A single script (build_trt_pipeline.py) runs all five stages. Benchmarked on Jetson AGX Thor Developer Kit (JetPack 7.2, MAXN power mode), GR00T-N1.7-LIBERO/libero_10, 4 denoising steps, 1 camera, batch size 1.

# PyTorch reference python scripts/deployment/standalone_inference_script.py \ --model-path checkpoints/GR00T-N1.7-LIBERO/libero_10 \ --dataset-path demo_data/libero_demo \ --embodiment-tag LIBERO_PANDA \ --traj-ids 0 1 2 3 4 --inference-mode pytorch --execution-horizon 8 \ --save-plot-path ./output/pytorch_inference.png # Optimized TensorRT engines python scripts/deployment/standalone_inference_script.py \ --model-path checkpoints/GR00T-N1.7-LIBERO/libero_10 \ --dataset-path demo_data/libero_demo \ --embodiment-tag LIBERO_PANDA \ --traj-ids 0 1 2 3 4 --inference-mode trt_full_pipeline --execution-horizon 8 \ --trt-engine-path ./gr00t_trt_optimized_mixed_nvfp4/engines \ --save-plot-path ./output/trt_nvfp4_inference.png

Left to interpreter shutdown, which frees module globals in an arbitrary order, the C++ destructors intermittently hang or segfault after the results have already printed. The patch therefore releases the engines explicitly at the end of main(), the same way benchmark_inference.py and verify_n1d7_trt.py already did, so this script now exits cleanly with status 0.

Deploy NVIDIA’s Isaac GR00T 1.7 Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor with TensorRT mixed NVFP4 quantization, taking end-to-end inference from 125 ms down to 39.9 ms, a 3.1x speedup at 25 Hz, with no measurable loss in task success.
